liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer says it started well, then Jerry lost concentration, leading to about twelve minutes of mess; Reviewer recalls the melody, key and rhythm dissolving into free music before the band pulled it back together [11][16]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Reviewer says Garcia played the opener poorly in every respect [11]
- **New Speedway Boogie** (1 review): Reviewer loved the guitar work on this song [15]
- **That Would Be Something** (1 review): Reviewer heard the second set years later and felt they should have been there [20]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): Reviewer found Jerry unusually soulful here, despite appearing unwell, and still remembers it [15]
- **Drumz** (1 review): Reviewer considers the drums segment the best ever played and imagines it frightening for people on psychedelics [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-06-02.nak300.bowen.116927.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 169 min [1]
- **gd95-06-02.sbd.583.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 3.86/5 by 55 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard sound quality very good; Reviewer calls the soundboard recording exceptional, with Weir clearly audible; Reviewer finds the recording quality amazing for a 1995 show [11][12][14][18]
- **gd1995-06-02.sbd.damico.92520.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1995-06-02.sbd.miller.114337.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer got a ticket from a friend, drove from Oakland in a camper with a crew, stopping at a bar after laughing hard [10]
- Reviewer attended, driving in from Santa Cruz, but missed the last night of the run [13]
- Reviewer says this was their last show, with remarkable energy in the room [15]
- Reviewer says it was the last time they saw the band with Jerry [16]
- Reviewer did not attend, having just returned to the Bay Area from overseas, and regrets it [20]
- Reviewer found the Shoreline vibe good, and Jerry looked five years older than at the spring Spectrum show [21]
- Weir played acoustic, and Gyoto Monks are credited as other artists [1]
- Reviewer felt the show sounded much like 1985 at the time [10]
- Reviewer rates it somewhat above average for 1995, though low on energy [12]
- Reviewer calls it their last really great show, with five more before Jerry died, and a favorite of the Vince era [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-06-02.nak300.bowen.116927.flac16**: taped by Jeff Bowen; transferred by Brad Foster; source: Source: Nakamichi cm300/cp1's > Sony TCD-D7; [1]. Also: Nak300 recording from Bowen, shared by Jeff from his master transfer; discs extracted in secure mode [1]
- **gd95-06-02.sbd.583.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CD > extracted on a Mac using Toast Audio Extractor (overlap)> SHN (note corrected info) [2]
- **gd1995-06-02.sbd.damico.92520.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: SBD > ? [3]. Also: Soundboard from a found box of analog and DAT tapes, uploaded by Joe, alongside first and second generation audience recordings [3]
- **gd1995-06-02.sbd.miller.114337.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat (44.1k) [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Shoreline Amphitheatre - June 3, 1995](https://www.dead.net/show/june-3-1995) [26]
